claim: Middle age represents a critical period of accelerated brain changes.
source: Middle age represents a critical period of accelerated brain changes and provides a window for early detection and intervention in age-related neurological decline.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about middle age.

claim: Middle age provides a window for early detection and intervention in age-related neurological decline.
source: Middle age represents a critical period of accelerated brain changes and provides a window for early detection and intervention in age-related neurological decline.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a consequence of middle age being a critical period.

claim: Hearing loss is a key early marker of age-related neurological decline.
source: Hearing loss is a key early marker of such decline and is linked to numerous comorbidities in older adults.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established relationship.

claim: Hearing loss is linked to numerous comorbidities in older adults.
source: Hearing loss is a key early marker of such decline and is linked to numerous comorbidities in older adults.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established relationship.

claim: Approximately 10% of middle-aged individuals who report hearing difficulties show normal audiograms.

claim: Cochlear neural degeneration (CND) could contribute to hidden hearing deficits.
source: Cochlear neural degeneration (CND) could contribute to these hidden hearing deficits, though its role remains unclear due to a lack of objective diagnostics and uncertainty regarding its perceptual outcomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a hypothesis.

claim: The role of CND in hidden hearing deficits remains unclear due to a lack of objective diagnostics and uncertainty regarding its perceptual outcomes.
source: Cochlear neural degeneration (CND) could contribute to these hidden hearing deficits, though its role remains unclear due to a lack of objective diagnostics and uncertainty regarding its perceptual outcomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a limitation in current understanding.

claim: Envelope following responses (EFRs) are neural ensemble responses to sound originating from the peripheral auditory pathway.
source: We measured envelope following responses (EFRs) – neural ensemble responses to sound originating from the peripheral auditory pathway – in young and middle-aged adults with normal audiograms and compared these responses to young and middle-aged Mongolian gerbils, where CND was histologically confirmed.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a definition of EFRs.

claim: Near-identical changes in EFRs were observed across human and gerbil species that were associated with CND.
source: We observed near-identical changes in EFRs across species that were associated with CND.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the cross-species comparison.

claim: Age-related speech-in-noise deficits were observed under challenging conditions.
source: Behavioral assessments revealed age-related speech-in-noise deficits under challenging conditions, while pupil-indexed listening effort increased with age even when behavioral performance was matched.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a behavioral finding.

claim: Pupil-indexed listening effort increased with age even when behavioral performance was matched.
source: Behavioral assessments revealed age-related speech-in-noise deficits under challenging conditions, while pupil-indexed listening effort increased with age even when behavioral performance was matched.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from pupillometry measurements.

claim: CND contributes to speech perception difficulties in midlife.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that CND contributes to speech perception difficulties and elevated listening effort in midlife, which may ultimately lead to listening fatigue and social withdrawal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study.

claim: CND contributes to elevated listening effort in midlife.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that CND contributes to speech perception difficulties and elevated listening effort in midlife, which may ultimately lead to listening fatigue and social withdrawal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study.

claim: CND may ultimately lead to listening fatigue and social withdrawal.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that CND contributes to speech perception difficulties and elevated listening effort in midlife, which may ultimately lead to listening fatigue and social withdrawal.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a speculative consequence.

claim: 45 million adults in the United States over 50 years of age have age-related hearing loss significant enough to interfere with communication.
source: Age-related hearing loss, defined as declines in hearing sensitivity, is exceedingly common; according to some estimates, 45 million adults in the United States over 50 years of age have age-related hearing loss that is significant enough to interfere with communication (Lin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Untreated hearing loss decreases quality of life.
source: Untreated hearing loss decreases quality of life and is considered to be the single-largest modifiable risk factor in middle age for other age-related comorbidities such as cognitive impairment and dementia (Livingston et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Untreated hearing loss is considered to be the single-largest modifiable risk factor in middle age for cognitive impairment and dementia.
source: Untreated hearing loss decreases quality of life and is considered to be the single-largest modifiable risk factor in middle age for other age-related comorbidities such as cognitive impairment and dementia (Livingston et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Current measures of hearing sensitivity fail to capture critical aspects of real-world listening challenges in the population with age-related hearing loss.

claim: Hearing difficulties experienced by up to 10% of adults seeking help in the hearing clinic are 'hidden' to current diagnostic procedures.

claim: Peripheral deafferentation caused by cochlear neural degeneration (CND) may underlie many perceptual difficulties.

claim: Postmortem studies using human temporal bones estimate a 40% deafferentation caused by CND by the fifth decade of life.

claim: CND causes neural coding deficits in the peripheral auditory pathway, affecting the faithful representation of spectrotemporally complex auditory stimuli.

claim: The evidence linking CND with perceptual deficits is mixed.
source: However, the evidence linking CND with perceptual deficits is mixed – current assessments of perceptual deficits associated with CND primarily focus on behavioral measures of speech in noise listening ability, with mixed evidence of deficits in individuals with putative CND (Prendergast et al., 2017a; Guest et al., 2017; Grant et al., 2020; Grant et al., 2022).

claim: Many noninvasive markers of CND have been proposed and validated in animal models.
source: First, while many noninvasive markers of CND have been proposed and validated in animal models (Kujawa and Liberman, 2009; Shaheen et al., 2015; Valero et al., 2018; Mehraei et al., 2016), noninvasive estimates of putative CND in humans cannot be confirmed with histological assessment of synapses in the same participants.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Noninvasive estimates of putative CND in humans cannot be confirmed with histological assessment of synapses in the same participants.
source: First, while many noninvasive markers of CND have been proposed and validated in animal models (Kujawa and Liberman, 2009; Shaheen et al., 2015; Valero et al., 2018; Mehraei et al., 2016), noninvasive estimates of putative CND in humans cannot be confirmed with histological assessment of synapses in the same participants.

claim: Cross-species comparative studies and computational modeling provide promising avenues for overcoming the gap in confirming CND in humans.

claim: The most promising tests for CND are ones with no linguistic context and short spectrotemporal processing windows.

claim: Behavioral readouts may minimize subliminal changes in perception that are reflected in listening effort but not in accuracies.

claim: Two individuals may show similar accuracies on a listening task, but one individual may need to exert substantially more listening effort to achieve the same accuracy as the other.

claim: CND was associated with decreased neural coding fidelity in middle-aged adults with normal audiometric thresholds.
source: Here, we used a cross-species approach, combined with simultaneous measurements of behavior and listening effort, to show that CND was associated with decreased neural coding fidelity and increased listening effort in middle-aged adults with normal audiometric thresholds.

claim: CND was associated with increased listening effort in middle-aged adults with normal audiometric thresholds.

claim: Putative CND was measured using the envelope following response (EFR) to rapid (~1000 Hz) modulation frequencies.

claim: Decreases in EFRs were selective only for responses with generators in the auditory nerve.
